conviction_note: Q3 is pinned to the company's own ~$575m adjusted EBITDA guide and US HRC kept rising through September, so a small Q3 beat and a Q4 guide above Q3 look likely; the print should trade on the Q4 number and on the 2027 fixed-price contract resets. Against that sit the Stelco/Ottawa fight and tariff headlines that took the stock down 6.3% in five days. Call skew (-15.6) and 13.9% of float short lean the same way as the fundamentals, so p_up is 56, not higher. The findings sum (+1.9) and the scaled number (+1.56) agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of about $575m, the company's own guide from the Q2 release (8-K ex99.1, 2026-07-23: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000764065/000076406526000097/clf-202606308xkex991.htm). Q4 was guided qualitatively as 'expected to exceed' Q3. Street EPS for Q3 is $0.19-0.23 (Yahoo $0.23 from 8 analysts, Benzinga $0.22, Earnings Agent via iTiger $0.19) and revenue $5.47-5.72B. These come from aggregators and do not fully agree, so the EBITDA guide is the bar. One sell-side summary says 2H26 consensus EBITDA is about $1.3B, which implies roughly $725m for Q4 (https://parameter.io/cleveland-cliffs-clf-shares-rise-as-wells-fargo-sees-2026-2027-earnings-beating-estimates/); 2027 consensus is about $2.3B.
positioning_check: Short interest 78.5m shares, 13.89% of float, 4.7 days to cover (MarketBeat, settlement 2026-09-30, published 2026-10-09, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/CLF/short-interest/). Earlier, ShortSqueeze showed 81.1m and 3.8 DTC as of 2026-08-27. 25-delta skew is -15.6 vol points, so upside calls are bid; put/call OI is 0.59. Event implied move is 10.55%, ATM IV 104.8%. Into the print the stock is -6.28% over 5 days and -2.68% over 20 days, 24.8% below its 52-week high. Only about 25% of analysts rate it Buy. The crowded short plus call-bid skew argue against sizing negatives large.

findings.finding: US HRC spot kept rising after the July guide was set. Nucor's consumer spot price was $1,130-1,135/st in July (SMU 2026-07-06/13/20), $1,160 on 2026-08-10, $1,190 on 2026-09-08, $1,220 by 2026-09-28 and +$10 again on 2026-10-05. Kallanish had domestic HRC at $1,210-1,220/st on 2026-09-25 against $825-865 a year earlier. Lead times are stretched. Cliffs' Q3 guide assumed only about +$55/t ASP over Q2's $1,124 and +300kt of shipments. So the spot-linked and monthly-index part of the book supports Q3 at or slightly above $575m, and a Q4 guide above the implied ~$725m consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is what this name trades on. 2026-07-23 rose +15.98% on the Q3 $575m guide despite an EPS miss. 2025-10-20 rose +21.47%. 2026-02-09 fell -16.43% on a miss and a weak outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: HRC is public, so the series is partly priced. The stock, though, is 24.8% off its high and fell 6.3% in five days on tariff and Stelco headlines, not on pricing. If the market had priced a Q4 step-up from ~$1,220 spot, CLF would be tracking NUE and STLD; instead it fell 4% on 10-15 while they fell 1%. The lag from spot to Cliffs' contract book means the Q4 guide carries information the Q3 number does not.
findings.independence: Same price series from a different outlet: gmk.center 2026-09-29 and 2026-10-06 (https://gmk.center/en/news/nucor-has-raised-the-price-of-hot-rolled-coils-to-1-230-per-tonne/amp/). Steel Dynamics' Q3 guide independently cites higher realised prices (separate finding). All of this is a proxy; the company has not updated its guide since July.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-06 Wells Fargo (Tanners) upgraded CLF to Overweight with a $14 target. The note says 2H26 and 2027 EBITDA will 'materially exceed' consensus: 2027 at $2.65B against roughly $2.3B consensus, even if HRC falls to about $1,000/st. Named drivers are repricing about 2Mt/yr of open fixed-price contracts (~$500m), lower discounts on about 6Mt of CRU-linked contracts (~$240m), and Stelco pricing. Last October's call carried the fixed-price contract resets, and management already said in July that 2027 resets are higher.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 print (2025-10-20) rose +21.47% when management discussed contract renegotiations and the forward outlook. 2026-07-23 rose +15.98% on forward commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: The note is public, and the stock rose only about 1% on it, to $12.30, then fell back to $12.165. Consensus still sits near $2.3B for 2027 and only a quarter of analysts rate it Buy. If the market believed the contract-reset math, the stock would sit near the $14 target, not below the pre-upgrade price.
findings.independence: Management's own July commentary: higher fixed-price contract resets and Stelco improvement drive 2027, with a 2027 EBITDA figure of about $3.3B cited by IndustryWeek (https://www.industryweek.com/leadership/companies-executives/news/55393737/cleveland-cliffs-sees-much-stronger-second-half-more-growth-into-27). That is a different source but the same underlying claim about contract resets.

findings.finding: Peer pre-guides set after Cliffs last spoke point to strong Q3 flat-rolled pricing with mixed beats. Steel Dynamics (2026-09-17) guided Q3 EPS to $5.34-5.38, against $3.69 in Q2, on record steel shipments, wider metal margins, higher realised prices and low customer inventories, with automotive among the solid end markets. Nucor (2026-09-17) guided $5.55-5.65, below a ~$5.99-6.17 consensus, but its steel mills earned more on higher selling prices with stable volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No CLF-specific history on a peer read-through. CLF's Q3 is itself pre-guided, so the reported quarter alone has rarely moved it; the guide has.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: both pre-guides are a month old. The residual is that STLD is an EAF and spot-heavy mill while Cliffs' contract book lags spot, so the margin gain shows up at Cliffs a quarter later, in the Q4 guide. That is not visible in CLF's 20-day run-up of -2.7%.
findings.independence: Nucor guidance: https://finviz.com/news/393374/nucor-announces-guidance-for-the-third-quarter-of-2026-earnings and the TIKR read that it missed consensus (https://www.tikr.com/blog/nucor-stock-estimates-bake-in-a-60-earnings-rebound-but-q3-guidance-just-missed). It rests partly on the same HRC trend as finding 1.

findings.finding: Stelco/Ottawa dispute. On 2026-09-29 Cliffs announced it would indefinitely idle cold-rolled and coated lines at Hamilton (wind-down from 10-09, up to 500 jobs; Stelco demand fell about 25% in Q2 2026 against the 2024 average). Ottawa says this breaches the 2024 Investment Canada Act undertakings: Joly's letter of 10-05 gave five business days and threatened a court order, penalties or a forced sale. Stelco replied that it is not in breach and the layoffs proceed. Goncalves said he is ready for court and would sell Stelco 'for a good offer'. CLF fell 9% on 09-28 and 4% on 10-15 while NUE and STLD fell about 1-2%. The call will have to address it, along with any idling charges.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print on a Stelco legal dispute. The headline days themselves moved CLF -9% (2026-09-28) and -4% (2026-10-15) against its peers, so the stock is sensitive to this line between prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced already: the stock gave up about 6% in five days on it. What is unpriced is the call's framing. A quantified idling charge, a court filing, or a sale price for Stelco (the company said the move changes mix, not tonnage) could swing either way. A sale at a good price would deleverage a $7.7B-debt balance sheet.
findings.independence: SteelOrbis 2026-09-29 on the idling (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/cleveland-cliffs-stelco-to-idle-hamilton-finishing-operations-due-to-us-tariffs-1480559.htm); CTV 2026-10-14 on the forced-sale threat (https://www.ctvnews.ca/business/article/everything-is-on-the-table-canada-weighs-legal-action-over-possible-stelco-layoffs/); 24/7 Wall St 2026-10-15 on the relative drop (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/15/cleveland-cliffs-drops-4-as-tariff-doubt-returns-nucor-and-steel-dynamics-slip/). The sign is two-sided, so the size is small.

findings.finding: Management said about half of the +300kt Q3 shipment step-up would come from automotive. Omdia's North America production tracker has Q3 2026 output pacing down about 0.6% (July +5.4% on the model-year 2027 start), with Mexico losing ground. That is a modest risk to the auto half of the volume assumption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Auto weakness drove the weak 2H24 prints. The volume miss on 2026-02-09 coincided with -16.43%.
findings.source_date: 2026-08 (Omdia tracker, July data; paywalled, headline/summary only)
findings.why_not_priced: Industry production is public, and a -0.6% pace is a small deviation. This would only matter if Cliffs misses the +300kt by much. It is a proxy, not confirmed by the company or a direct customer.
findings.independence: None directly; IndustryWeek (2026-07-23) is the source for the auto share of the step-up. The Steel Dynamics guide calls automotive demand solid, which cuts against this finding.

findings.finding: Canada doubled its counter-surtax on affected US-origin steel goods from 25% to 50% effective 2026-09-08 (C$4.57B of basic and semi-finished steel). That raises the cost of Cliffs' US-mill shipments into Canada in late Q3 and Q4, while further shielding Stelco's domestic market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this line specifically. Trade-policy days moved CLF more than its peers (09-28, 10-15).
findings.why_not_priced: It was announced publicly in September, and its net effect on Cliffs is two-sided and small. This is filed for completeness. EY and CH Robinson summaries describe US steel as exempt from Canada's TRQ, a separate measure, so the two are not contradictory, but the claim rests on one secondary source.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print favours upside asymmetry. 13.89% of float is short (4.7 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30); call skew is -15.6 vol points; the stock fell 6.3% in the five sessions before the print on headline risk; only about 25% of analysts rate it Buy. A guide or contract-reset surprise meets a crowded short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Large upside moves on forward-looking beats (+15.98%, +21.47%, +12.45%) came with similarly elevated short interest.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew already says the market leans up, so this finding agrees with the price and is sized small. What it adds is the squeeze mechanism on a good guide.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline's skew and run-up come from Yahoo options and chart data, a different source.

outside_window.finding: Steel Dynamics reports Q3 after the close on 2026-10-19, and Nucor on 2026-10-26. Read-throughs from those calls land after CLF's exit window.
Any Canadian superior-court application under the Investment Canada Act, seeking penalties or a forced sale of Stelco, has no filing date; none had been filed as of 2026-10-11.
The POSCO strategic partnership remains an MOU. The definitive-agreement timeline has slipped past 1H26 and management says it is not in a hurry.

searched_and_found_nothing: Blast-furnace outages or idlings at US Cliffs facilities in Jul-Oct 2026: the SMU blast-furnace status page and Argus results were old or undated, and nothing dated 2026 was found beyond the June Dearborn restart musing
Detroit Three Q3 2026 production halts or UAW disruption: no 2026 items found

EDGAR filings since 2026-07-23: only director retainer Form 4s (10-02, 07-02), a State Street 13G and the 07-24 8-K naming Celso Goncalves Jr. President/CFO; no notes offering, redemption or open-market insider buy
A sourced sell-side Q3 EBITDA consensus distinct from the company guide: not found (YCharts empty); EPS/revenue consensus only from aggregators
POSCO definitive agreement news Aug-Oct 2026: none

rejected_candidates.candidate: SMU's average HRC price of about $1,300/st as of 2026-09-22 (via gmk.center), against Kallanish's $1,210-1,220
rejected_candidates.detail: The same HRC trend as finding 1. The two price levels disagree by about $80, so finding 1 uses the Nucor CSP and Kallanish figures.

baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the call-bid skew (-15.6) and the crowded short. It cuts against the -6.3% five-day run-down, which I attribute to the Stelco and tariff headlines rather than to the pricing line, so the lean is up but p_up stays at 56.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 / 5: the HRC finding lands partly inside the company's own Q3 guide and is a proxy, so it was cut from +1.5 to +1.2, keeping only the Q4-guide part.
Lesson 5 (sell-side note is public) and lesson 1: the Wells Fargo/contract-reset finding was cut from +1.0 to +0.8.
Lesson 5: the peer pre-guides are a month old and mixed (Nucor below consensus), so cut from +0.5 to +0.3.

Lesson 7: the Stelco negative sits against call skew and 13.9% short interest and its sign is two-sided, so cut from -0.5 to -0.4. The auto-production proxy was cut from -0.5 to -0.3 (lesson 5; STLD calls auto solid). The Canada counter-tariff proxy was cut from -0.3 to -0.2.

Lesson 8 and the core guidance row: a guide-driven print on a name with a 14.1% median reaction raised abs_move_pct from 12 to 13, and p_up went from 55 to 56 because the positives rest partly on a company guide.
